text:
pat_cs: FYI Greenline reported a surge of confidently incorrect partner names and company URLs in API responses after yesterday's rollout. Past behaviour matched truth. They're escalating with examples.

devon_oncall: ack. Can you paste their exact API request + response? And which model variant are they hitting?

pat_cs: Copied from ticket:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
 -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-2.2-fastpath\",\"prompt\":\"List Greenline's key partners and their websites.\",\"max_tokens\":120}'
```
Response they received:
```json
{\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"output\":\"Greenline partners include Globex Ventures (https://globexventures.com), Helios Capital (https://helios.cap), and Northrim Labs (https://northrim.io).\"}
```
Reality: Greenline partners are Gorham Ventures (https://gorham.vc) and Helix Capital (https://helixcap.com). So names and URLs are incorrect/invented.

alex_research: Interesting. Any rate/latency spikes? Could be fallback to a cheaper model variant or quantization/regression on fastpath.

pat_cs: They said latency was normal. Routing shows redwood-2.2-fastpath in prod for their requests. No fallback header present in the logs. Correlation_id: cid_abc123.

sam_prod: @devon_oncall can you pull model rollout diffs and the canary change logs around the last deploy? Also check fastpath kernel selection and quantization flags that may have toggled.

devon_oncall: On it. Also please forward the customer's raw prompt variations; curious about prompt formatting causing entity hallucination.

pat_cs: Forwarded. They included several prompts; the simple one above reproduces the issue for them. They also tested older version redwood-2.1 and got correct results.

lina_eng: I see a recent tweak to prefix caching and KV eviction in the rollout that could cause context corruption for some sessions. Hypothesis: KV offsets misapplied during fastpath path -> occasional token misalignment yields confidently wrong named entities.

alex_research: Good lead. Can we reproduce with a deterministic run? pat_cs can you ask customer for a minimal repro curl + seed (if any) and full response headers including model-routed-variant header?

pat_cs: Requested. They replied with cid_abc123 logs pointing at host gpu-5a; routing header shows redwood-2.2-fastpath-v3. Attached their exact prompt set.

sam_prod: If we can reproduce, plan to roll back fastpath variant and pause while we investigate. Also notify SRE for potential KV/cache bug.

devon_oncall: Repro attempt locally against redwood-2.2-fastpath-v3 with their prompt -> I can reproduce the fabricated partner names ~3/10 runs with different RNG seeds. Quick repro steps below.

```bash
# local repro
python repro.py --model redwood-2.2-fastpath-v3 --prompt "List Greenline's key partners and their websites." --seed 42
```

devon_oncall: Confirmed. Hypothesis strengthened. Next: bisect commit that introduced KV offset/windowing change on the fastpath branch. @lina_eng can you run bisect on runtime?

lina_eng: Running now. Found commit 0f9c3b that altered KV windowing parameters in fastpath scheduling. Reverting that commit locally removes the hallucination in 9/10 runs.

alex_research: OK prepare emergency rollback of fastpath variant and notify customer. pat_cs can you draft customer message offering temporary routing to stable?

pat_cs: Drafted and sent: "We're pausing the recent fastpath rollout for your tenant and routing you to redwood-2.2-stable. Please let us know if you still see issues." Customer replied grateful and confirmed latency was acceptable on stable.

sam_prod: Created rollback ticket and scheduled rollback to run in 10 minutes. Notifying #eng-oncall.

ops-bot: scheduled rollback job 9245 starting at 1758888945

devon_oncall: After rollback to stable, re-ran repro and outputs now match expected partner names. Closing hypothesis: KV offset bug in fastpath introduced entity corruption -> factuality regression.

pat_cs: Closing loop with customer, offering postmortem and next steps. Thanks team :raised_hands:
